g1.name: Architectural hubs
g1.prompt: In the repository at {REPO}, name the three most connected symbols (the architectural hubs) and the file each one is defined in. Give the three as a short list.

truth.source: graphify god-nodes --top 3 --json against the repository graph

g2.name: Definition and caller
g2.prompt: In the repository at {REPO}, which file defines the class Verifier, and which function calls it? Answer with the file path and the calling function.

truth.source: graphify affected "Verifier" --depth 1 against the repository graph

tool_card:
graphify 0.9.61 is installed on this machine and the repository's graph is already built. Run it from the repository root:

  "{GRAPHIFY}" <command>

Commands: query "<question>" [--budget N], path "A" "B", explain "X", affected "X" [--depth N], god-nodes [--top N] [--json]. The default graph is graphify-out/graph.json in the folder you run it from; pass --graph for another. Indexing and querying are local: they parse the code and read the graph file, and call no model.
delivery: Answer the question directly. Do not create or modify any files, and do not use the Skill tool.
limit_plain: Your entire answer must be at most 400 tokens.
notes: The four other harnesses (surface, proxy, wrapper, goal) deliver the same base pipeline text through different mechanisms; base_graph stands for all four, and super_graph adds the ten-pass chain on top.

The 400-token ceiling reaches the harness arms as the repository's own /token limit 400 command, which the hook turns into rule 15. The bare arms get the same ceiling as a plain sentence. Comparing compliance between the two is part of the point.
Ground truth comes from the graph itself, so an answer is scored against what the code actually contains rather than against an opinion.

bare_strict exists because the first run showed the control was not clean: graphify is installed on this machine, so agents given no tool card discovered and used it anyway. bare_nograph therefore measures 'not told about it', and bare_strict measures 'cannot use it'.
forbid_line: Do not use graphify or any pre-built graph, and do not read graphify-out/. Answer from the source files themselves.
